statHelp.class: The ship class, decided automatically by how much of the structure budget goes to cargo, pressurized (passenger) space and combat parts.
statHelp.mob: How fast the ship travels: total engine power divided by mass, times a fixed factor. More power or less mass raises it.
statHelp.crg: How much cargo the ship can carry, from every installed cargo hold.
statHelp.min: How much ore the ship can mine per trip, from every installed mining rig.
statHelp.hp: Total hit points from every installed part. Lost in combat, restored by repair.
statHelp.pot: Total thrust from every installed engine. Feeds mobility.
statHelp.pdf: Combat damage output from every installed weapon.
statHelp.bli: Reduces the damage of each hit that gets through the shield.
statHelp.esc: Absorbs damage first in a fight, before armor or the hull take any. Regenerates a little each combat round. Draws Combat power from the battery — with no battery to power it, it can't be installed.
statHelp.sen: Spots ambushes early, lowering the chance of being surprised in an encounter.
statHelp.mass: Total weight of every installed part (plus a loaded tank's fuel, where that adds weight). Pulls mobility down.
statHelp.fuelCap: How much fuel the ship can hold, from every installed tank.
statHelp.fuelUse: How much fuel is burned per unit of travel.
statHelp.energyCont: Continuous power balance: reactor/solar generation minus everything that always draws power (sensors, life support, mining rigs...). Must stay at zero or above, or the ship can't fly — separate from Combat power below, and never drawn from the battery.
statHelp.energyCombat: Total combat-only power draw from every installed weapon and shield (always zero or negative). Covered by the battery's charge and output, never by Cruising power or the reactor — see Battery capacity / Battery output.
statHelp.batCharge: Total energy the battery can store for combat. Must cover the ship's whole Combat power draw, or weapons/shields can't be installed.
statHelp.batOutput: The most energy the battery can deliver in a single round. Must cover the ship's whole Combat power draw per round, or weapons/shields can't be installed.
statHelp.batInput: How fast the battery recharges between fights.
statHelp.autonomy: How far a full tank takes the ship, in route-distance units (the same units as route lengths). Below it: how many of the world's routes that covers.
statHelp.condition: Average wear across every installed part, from 100% (new) down.
statHelp.structure: How much of the structure budget the bridge sets is used by everything else installed.

placement.exhaust: Parts are behind this engine's exhaust — turn it or move it to the back edge of the ship.
placement.facing: Parts are in this weapon's line of fire — turn it or move it to the edge of the ship.

warnings.grant: Adds credits to the player's wallet. Recorded in the audit log.
warnings.remove: Removes credits from the wallet (cannot go below zero).
warnings.clear: Sets a negative balance back to zero.
warnings.password: Sets a new password for this account and signs it out everywhere. The password itself is never recorded in the audit log.
warnings.unstick: Expires the ship's active mission and parks the ship in port. Its future route presence is deleted.
warnings.ban: Suspends the account at once and ends all sessions. Admin accounts cannot be banned.
warnings.reset: Wipes parts, materials, repairs, missions and sessions, returns the ship to the home port and re-applies the starter kit and credits. History is kept. This cannot be undone.
warnings.fastOps: Per player: this player's missions, trips, scavenging, mining and repairs finish in a few seconds (admin.debug_fast_ops_seconds) while the UI still shows the real durations. Takes effect on the next job started.

admin.mismatch: Replay DIVERGES from the stored log

connectorRules.notConfigured: Not configured: parts of this type get universal connectors until rules are set.
connectorRules.weightHelp: Relative weights per side (0 = never). One kind is rolled per side when a part is generated; the result never changes afterwards. Engines/weapons: side W must stay none.
connectorRules.forbidden: Forbidden combinations (a roll matching every chosen side is rejected)
connectorRules.oneKindPerPart: One kind per part (all connected sides use the same kind, ports at the same place on every side)
connectorRules.diagram: Connector kinds allowed on each side
connectorRules.noPortHelp: To make a side sometimes bare, allow the dash (none) on it and give it a weight: 1 against 3 for central means a 25% chance of no port on that side. At least the minimum number of sides always keeps a port.

parts.partType: The part's permanent code (used by saves and the catalog). Lowercase with underscores; it cannot be changed after creation.
parts.displayName: What players see in menus, the market and reports, in both languages.
parts.description: The short blurb on the part's card and popup, in both languages.
parts.partClass: What the part does for the ship. Bridge is required, engines move it, weapons/defense fight, cargo carries, and so on. Engines and weapons also have a facing (see connector rules).
parts.rarity: How rare the part is: sets its colour, how often it appears in shops and drops, and which ship formats it can unlock.
parts.mass: Weight in tonnes. Heavier ships are slower (mobility = thrust ÷ mass).
parts.structureCost: How much of the ship's structure budget this part uses. Bridges use a negative number: they PROVIDE the budget.
parts.basePrice: The shop price of a brand-new part in credits, before location and condition adjustments.
parts.scrapValue: What the part is worth as scrap when it is broken beyond use.
parts.partHp: Hit points of this part itself, used when parts take damage.
parts.pot: Potential output: engine thrust. Divided by the ship's total mass it gives mobility.
parts.pdf: Point defense fire: the part's firepower in combat.
parts.bli: Build integrity: armor that cuts damage taken.
parts.esc: Escape/shield rating: absorbs damage before it reaches the armor and hull.
parts.sen: Sensor rating: how well the ship detects ambushes and enemies.
parts.min: Mining output: needed for mining missions and jobs.
parts.energyCont: Continuous energy: positive generates power, negative draws it all the time. The ship's total must stay at or above zero to fly.
parts.energyCombat: Energy drawn per combat round by this part (negative) — batteries must cover it.
parts.fuelCap: Fuel tank capacity this part adds.
parts.fuelUse: Fuel an engine burns per 100 distance (empty for parts that do not burn fuel; ion engines use 0).
parts.batCharge: How much energy this battery stores for combat.
parts.batOutput: How much energy this battery can deliver each combat round.
parts.specialProp: Special abilities the part grants (passenger space, life support).
parts.connectorRules: How the ports of a NEW part of this type are generated. The result is fixed on the part forever; changing the rules only affects parts made afterwards.

materials.displayName: Name shown to players, both languages.
materials.rarity: How rare the ore is: drives how hard it is to find when mining.
materials.basePrice: What the material sells for at a typical port (before location and mood).

factions.id: The faction's permanent code. Art files and missions are tied to it.
factions.displayName: Name shown to players, both languages.
factions.description: The faction's pitch on the selection screen, both languages.
factions.color: The faction colour (hex, like #4a90d9) used on badges and the map.
factions.playable: Whether new players can choose this faction at the start. Off for NPC factions such as pirates.
factions.relations: How this faction treats each other faction. Hostile ones attack on sight; allies leave you alone; it also changes prices there.
factions.starterKitHint: Optional starter-kit suggestion for the faction (leave empty unless you know the format).

locations.id: The place's permanent code. Art files are tied to it.
locations.displayName: Name shown to players, both languages.
locations.description: Short description of the place, both languages.
locations.type: What kind of place it is (port, shipyard, outpost…). Mission templates use it to decide where they can be offered.
locations.zone: Danger zone of the place (0 = safe core, higher = more dangerous). Routes take the riskier end.
locations.factionId: The faction that controls the place: sets prices and how you are treated.
locations.isolation: Price multiplier for being remote (fuel, repairs, parts): 1 = normal, above 1 = more expensive.
locations.mood: Local price mood: below 1 is cheaper, above 1 is dearer.
locations.services: What the player can do here: buy parts, sell, repair, take missions, passengers.

routes.nodeBId: The other end (the pair must be unique and ordered).
routes.distance: Length of the route: sets travel time and fuel burned.
routes.danger: How dangerous the route is: raises encounter chances and rewards.

rescue.title: Ship adrift
rescue.body: Your ship ran out of fuel and is drifting. A tow brings it back to port — it costs credits and may leave your balance negative.

role.BRIDGE: Required. Every ship needs exactly one: it is the command core, keeps the pilot alive if the ship is destroyed, and sets how much structure the ship can carry.
role.ENGINE: Required: a ship with no engine cannot move. Chemical engines also need a fuel tank; ion engines need steady power instead.
role.TANK: Holds the fuel. Any ship with a chemical engine needs at least one, and a bigger tank means longer trips between refuels.
role.BATTERY: Stores energy for combat. Weapons and shields draw from it, so it must cover their demand or the ship is not allowed to fly.
role.REACTOR: Generates energy continuously. Engines and systems draw power all the time, so total generation must cover them.
role.WEAPON: Adds firepower. Needed for escort missions and to win fights; costs energy in combat.
role.DEFENSE: Adds armor, shield and hit points so the ship survives attacks. It adds no speed, cargo or firepower, and its mass slows you down.
role.CARGO: Adds cargo capacity. More cargo means bigger deliveries and better pay, but adds mass.
role.SENSOR: Spots trouble early, which lowers the chance of being ambushed on a route.
role.UTILITY: Special equipment that unlocks certain missions (mining rigs, life support, and so on).
